s1.syndrome_frame: a subacute breast syndrome with a palpable mass and spiculated lesion
salient_findings: palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
spiculated lesion on breast MRI with early enhancement peak
cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells on excisional biopsy
key_facts: 62-year-old woman
one-month history of burning sensation and discomfort in her left breast
no fever or systemic symptoms
hypertension
remote history of hemorrhoidectomy, dilation and curettage, colonoscopy, and gastroscopy
heavy smoker
3 × 3 cm palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
no axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
unremarkable routine blood tests, chest radiograph, and ECG
breast MRI showed an ill-defined, deep retroareolar spiculated lesion
excisional biopsy showed breast tissue containing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells
epithelial cells positive for cytokeratin AE1/E3 and negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, matches the description of a palpable mass and spiculated lesion on breast MRI

shortlist.label: Medullary carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: matches the description of a dense lymphoid infiltrate and negative estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu status

shortlist.label: Metaplastic carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: can present with a palpable mass and spiculated lesion, and may have a dense lymphoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: can present with a palpable mass and spiculated lesion, and may have a mix of epithelial and mesenchymal components

shortlist.label: Tubular carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: can present with a palpable mass and spiculated lesion, and may have a dense lymphoid infiltrate

raw.rationale: The presence of a dense lymphoid infiltrate and the epithelial cells being negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu are characteristic of medullary carcinoma of the breast

rejected.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific features and presence of lymphoid infiltrate is less common

rejected.label: Metaplastic carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: No evidence of metaplastic elements in the biopsy

rejected.label: Pleomorphic carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: No mention of pleomorphic cells or high-grade features

rejected.label: Tubular carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: Tubular carcinomas typically have a distinct tubular architecture and are often positive for estrogen receptor
